profile.name: Huaylía
profile.tagline: An Andean music and dance genre of Peru performed near Christmas and at takanakuy fights.
profile.insight: In Chumbivilcas, Peru, the lively rhythms of huaylía provide the traditional musical backdrop for the ritual takanakuy fights.
profile.profile: The huaylía or wayliya is a genre of Andean music and dance from Peru typically performed near Christmas. It originates from the central and southern highlands, spanning Apurímac, Ayacucho, Cusco, Huancavelica, and Junín. A prominent variant, huaylía de Chumbivilcas, achieved National Cultural Heritage status in 2016 and accompanies takanakuy fights.
profile.profile_long:
Huaylía, also spelled wayliya, is a traditional genre of Andean music and dance originating from Peru. Documentary records place its practice primarily across the central and southern highlands of the country. Specifically, the tradition is located within the departments of Apurímac, Ayacucho, Cusco, Huancavelica, and Junín. 

Performance of the huaylía is historically tied to the Christmas season, occurring typically near the holiday. Within the southern department of Cusco, a specific regional variant known as the huaylía de Chumbivilcas has developed. This variant received official recognition as a National Cultural Heritage in the year 2016. Furthermore, the music of huaylía de Chumbivilcas serves a distinct cultural role as the traditional soundtrack played during takanakuy fights.
